findings.summary: The notification reconciler's three production inputs are exercised only by stand-ins
findings.recommendation: Scope: class - every test of lib/bridge-notify.js supplies the reconciler's inputs itself, so the code that supplies them in production has no test. Three members, all added in this change: (1) server.js:12241 `bridgeNotify.setLaneReader(...)`, the only thing that turns real sessions, launch sequences and composed lanes into the `{sessionId, launchId, receiptSeq, availability}` entries `_fleetIdle` judges. It sits inside `require.main === module`, so no test can reach it; test/bridge-notify.test.js replaces `_deps.lanes` with literal objects carrying an `availability` string. Ruling 8's substance (fresh receipt, of the current launch, engine at rest, stale or unknown is not idle) is therefore proven only for hand-written strings, never for a real expired receipt, a relaunched session whose newest receipt belongs to the previous launch, or a busy engine. (2) lib/bridge-api.js operatorSwitch writing `enabled.at`: the tests' `enable()` helper writes the setting directly, and no test asserts the operator route writes it. Deleting that line leaves every test green and makes `_since()` return null forever, so no notification is ever raised. (3) lib/bridge-gateway.js tick() calling `bridgeNotify.reconcile()`: no gateway test asserts a notification results from a tick. By reading, all three are currently wired correctly (the reader's `lane.composed.availability` and `lane.workload.receipt.seq` match what workload-fleet#laneFor and workload-compose#composeLane return; `received_at` and the fact `at` are both toISOString values, so the string comparison against `enabled.at` is sound). The gap is that nothing would fail if any of them stopped being so. Fix by construction rather than by three more stand-ins: move the lane reader out of the main-only block into an exported function that takes the activity observer (lib/workload-fleet.js is the natural home), and test it against real session, launch-sequence and workload-receipt rows for at least: fresh complete/safe-to-clear (idle), expired receipt, receipt of a previous launch, engine busy, and no launch sequence. Then one test that enables through POST /api/bridge/operator/enable, writes a blocked receipt and runs gateway.tick(), asserting the notification exists; that single test covers members 2 and 3.

findings.summary: fleet-idle identifies an episode by a digest of the current lane set, so one idle spell can notify repeatedly and a returning one not at all
findings.recommendation: Scope: instance - lib/bridge-notify.js `_fleetIdle` keys the notification on a digest of `sessionId:launchId:receiptSeq` for every lane instead of tracking when an episode begins and ends, and those are not the same thing as ruling 8's 'membership or state change ends the episode'. Two consequences. Over-notifying: a lane that stays complete and re-reports before its receipt expires (which the operational guide tells every session to do, at 120 minutes) writes a new receipt with a new seq; nothing about the fleet's state changed, but the digest did, so the operator is told the fleet is idle again, once per renewal per lane for as long as the spell lasts. `_workBlocked` deliberately suppresses exactly this case ('a lane that stays blocked and reports again is not a new event'); fleet-idle does not. Under-notifying: when the episode really does end and the fleet returns to the same set at the same receipts (a session launches and ends without the others reporting; a lane is held and released; an engine goes busy and rests without a new receipt), the digest is the one already used, so the new idle spell is silent, contrary to the module's own comment that 'a later idle spell is a new one'. The test 'tells the operator once per idle episode' only covers a lane that works and finishes and a membership shrink, so neither case is pinned. Either get the Architect to rule that a same-state renewal is a new episode and that A-B-A is the same one, and record it in docs/operator-bridge.md, or key the episode on its start: persist whether the fleet was idle on the previous pass and mint a new episode key only on the not-idle to idle transition. Add tests for a same-state renewal and for leaving and returning to the same set.

findings.summary: A faithful replay of a candidate submission is refused REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT once another candidate has been merged into it
findings.recommendation: Scope: instance - lib/bridge-api.js submitCandidate decides whether a repeated requestId carries the same payload by comparing the request's receipts with `bridgeStore.candidates.receipts(candidateId)`, and that list is not what was submitted: applyCandidateWrite's `carryReceiptsTo` adds the folded candidate's receipts to the survivor. After a merge, `had.length !== bound.length`, so the same launch replaying the same requestId with the identical payload gets 409 'already used by this launch for a different candidate', which is false, and ruling 4 requires the same payload to return the same candidate. A session retrying after a timeout would reasonably resubmit under a fresh id and create a duplicate of something the Master already merged. Compare against what the submission itself bound: either record the submitted payload's digest on the candidate row at creation and compare digests, or mark carried receipts as carried and exclude them. Add a test: submit A and B, merge B into A, replay A's request, expect 200 replayed. The rest of the comparison is exact as far as it matters: kind and text are compared by strict equality, receipts as a set of ids, and a list naming the same receipt twice is treated as naming it once.

findings.summary: A merge rewrites the survivor's receipt set, which is also the only record of what the survivor was submitted with
findings.recommendation: Scope: instance. bridge_candidate_receipts carries two meanings with nothing to tell them apart: what a session submitted, and what a merge carried on afterwards (applyCandidateWrite, carryReceiptsTo). Three readers then disagree about which it is. (1) submitCandidate's replay check in lib/bridge-api.js rebuilds 'same payload' from candidates.receipts(): once the Master merges A into B, the session that submitted B and retries its own requestId with its own unchanged payload gets had.length !== bound.length and a 409 REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT, against the doc's 'Repeating it with the same payload returns the same candidate'. (2) The carry changes what B rests on without bumping B's version, so an approve naming a version read before the merge is applied to a candidate whose receipts are no longer the ones that were read; the version check is the mechanism meant to refuse exactly that. (3) The JSDoc on candidates.receipts ('as recorded when it was submitted') and on _receiptsStillHold ('from the candidate's own project and launch') describe the pre-merge model; the code checks presence and digest only, and after a merge the carried receipts are another launch's by construction. States observed: submitted, approved, rejected, merged, plus 'submitted and merge survivor', which has no representation. Fix by giving the submitted payload its own source of truth (store a digest of kind + text + receipt ids on the candidate row at submit and compare the replay against that), bump the survivor's version in the same transaction as the carry, and either mark carried rows (a carried_from column) or delete the two JSDoc claims. No test covers a replayed submit of a merge survivor or an approve of the survivor at its pre-merge version.

findings.summary: The 'no backlog' and 'found again on the next pass' claims do not hold for fleet-idle or beyond the 24-hour lookback
findings.recommendation: Scope: instance (two claims, one doc section and one module header). docs/operator-bridge.md 'Server notifications' says 'Only events from after the bridge was last enabled are considered', and the lib/bridge-notify.js header says 'Only records written while the bridge is enabled are considered, so enabling it delivers no backlog'. _fleetIdle() takes no `since`: reconcile() calls it with the lanes' current receipts whatever their age, so enabling the bridge while the fleet is already idle on receipts written before the enable enqueues fleet-idle on the first pass. The no-backlog test in test/bridge-notify.test.js exercises work-blocked only. Separately, the doc's 'One that could not be enqueued is found again on the next pass' is true only inside LOOKBACK_MS: _since() floors at now minus 24 hours, so a work-blocked or operator-needed event whose enqueue fails, or whose pass does not run, for longer than that is never notified, and the constant's own comment ('anything older than this was either notified already or happened while the bridge was off') asserts otherwise. An operator reading the doc expects silence on enable and gets a post; a maintainer reading the header assumes one window bounds all three kinds. Decide which is intended and make one side match: either bound fleet-idle by the enable time (every member receipt received at or after `since`) with a test, or state in the doc and header that fleet-idle reports the current condition and is not subject to the window, and state the 24-hour bound where the doc promises a retry.

findings.summary: Undecided candidates and undelivered server notifications accumulate with no age-out now that Phase 3 gives them producers
findings.recommendation: Scope: class. Why it broke: the retention rule written before these producers existed (lib/bridge-store.js#prune, docs/operator-bridge.md 'never removed, whatever their age') keeps every `submitted` candidate and every `ready` routeless outbound item forever, and Phase 3 adds the writers that fill both. Members found: (1) bridge_candidates in state `submitted` - the cap MAX_OPEN_CANDIDATES_PER_LAUNCH bounds one launch at 5, but launches are unbounded and a launch that ends leaves its undecided candidates behind; candidates.list() is oldest-first capped at MAX_LIST (100) and listCandidates passes no paging, so `tc bridge candidates` leads with claims from ended launches and anything past the first 100 is not listed at all, which means the Master never sees a current candidate. (2) bridge_outbound rows of kind `notification` - lib/bridge-notify.js#reconcile enqueues one per blocked receipt, per escalated exchange and per idle episode on every enabled pass, and nothing acknowledges them while no helper exists (declared); outbound.ready() is oldest-first, so the first helper to attach posts days-old 'work is blocked' and 'fleet is waiting for work' statements that are no longer true, ahead of current replies. Search for other members: any bridge record prune() exempts by state rather than by age. Remedy is a construction in prune(), not a longer exemption list: age out a `submitted` candidate whose source launch has ended or which is older than a stated period (to an audited terminal state), and drop a `ready` notification older than a stated period with an audited reason, since a notification describes a condition and not a debt. If unbounded retention is the intended design for these two, record that decision and its consequence for the helper's first drain under ADR 0023 Decision 20, which currently says what remains is bounded.

observations.summary: A server restart while the fleet is idle announces fleet-idle again, contrary to the new doc claim
observations.recommendation: Scope: class - lib/bridge-notify.js _fleetIdle treats the first pass after process start as a true reading of the fleet, but the lane composition cannot read AVAILABLE until the activity observer has confirmed at-rest, and that takes longer than the first bridge pass. Timeline from the tree: lib/activity-observer.js TICK_MS is 10 s and AT_REST_OBSERVATIONS is 2, so a pane is at-rest no earlier than about 20 s after activityObserver.start(); server.js BRIDGE_TICK_MS is 15 s, so the first reconcile() runs at about 15 s, reads every finished lane as COMPLETE_NOT_CLEAR, and primes _state.episode to null. The next pass (about 30 s) reads AVAILABLE, sees key !== null episode, and enqueues a new notice under a fresh episode:<now> key. So each restart during an idle spell posts once more, and docs/operator-bridge.md 'A fleet that was already idle when ... the server started, is not announced' is false in production. The test 'does not announce a fleet that was already idle when the bridge was enabled or the server started' models the restart with _reset() and stand-in lanes that are AVAILABLE on the first read, and the new wiring test itself asserts the real reader is not AVAILABLE straight after load. Other members of the class, same cause (any transient non-AVAILABLE reading ends the episode): an observation older than FRESH_MS (30 s) when the observer's 3 s tick budget skips a pane, a capture timeout, and server.js _composedLane catching a compose failure and returning UNKNOWN; each ends the episode and re-announces on recovery. Enable at runtime is unaffected because the observer is warm. A fix would not prime on a pass where the reading is not yet trustworthy: prime only once every live lane has a fresh engine observation that is not unknown and not a first unconfirmed observation, or persist the episode key in bridge settings so a restart resumes it. ACCEPT is a reasonable disposition while the bridge is off by default and no helper exists; if accepted, the doc sentence about server start should be deleted rather than left asserting it.

observations.summary: expire() rejects and drops without an audit row, and an expired candidate is recorded as a plain rejection

A candidate expired by age becomes 'rejected' with a version bump and decided_at, no decided_generation and no bridge_audit row, so the only trace that the server and not the Master rejected it is the null decided_generation; the prior finding asked for an audited terminal state. Nothing in the route's progress reads the status item (tick() advances routes independently and only a delivered reply closes one), so no route is stuck by this, and the docs now state the 24-hour drop. Recorded so the choice is visible: a helper attaching after 24 hours to a still-open route posts no 'still waiting' line for it.

observations.summary: A fleet that first becomes idle before any pass has read it busy is taken as already idle and never announced
observations.recommendation: Scope: instance - lib/bridge-notify.js _fleetIdle primes on the first reading that is not `unknown` and, when that reading is `idle`, records the episode without a notice. Priming therefore stays open for as long as every pass reads `unknown`, which lib/workload-compose.js composeBase gives to any lane with no current receipt and an engine not seen busy (`no-current-receipt`: never reported, or a `complete` receipt older than the 120 minute expiry) and to a Master lane. If such a lane then reports `complete`/`safe-to-clear` without a 15 s bridge pass catching its engine busy, the first known reading is `idle` and the fleet's real transition into idle goes unannounced, however long after start it happens. The same holds for the last working lane finishing inside the roughly 20 s window after a restart in which no engine has been observed. Bounded: any pass that reads WORKING, WAITING, BLOCKED, HELD or STOPPED, or an empty fleet, primes with no episode and the next idle is announced, so work of ordinary length is unaffected. No test covers a long unprimed spell. ACCEPT is reasonable; a fix would bound the unprimed spell in time rather than wait indefinitely.

observations.summary: An open episode now ends only if a pass catches a busy reading, so work seen only as not-clear or unknown is folded into the old episode
observations.recommendation: Scope: class - with `unknown` no longer ending an episode, a lane that works and finishes again is re-announced only when some pass reads it WORKING/WAITING/BLOCKED/HELD/STOPPED. Members found by reading lib/workload-compose.js: (1) work whose engine-busy stretch falls between two 15 s passes, which the previous code caught through the COMPLETE_NOT_CLEAR spell that follows it; (2) a lane under an operator narrowing with forceUnknown, whose WAITING or BLOCKED is turned into UNKNOWN, so a wait or a block under narrowing does not end the episode. In both the fleet goes idle again under the same members and no notice is made. Lane leaving, lane relaunched under the same session id (new launch id, so the members string differs) and an empty fleet all end the episode correctly, including while another lane reads unknown. ACCEPT is reasonable: the trade was made deliberately to stop restart and lapse re-announcements, and the docs state it.

findings.summary: A route's expired status notice is raised again once retention removes its row
findings.recommendation: Scope: class - 'never raised again' rests on the dropped row still existing, and prune() deletes that row while the thing that caused it is still live. Confirmed member: the status notice. expire() drops it 24 hours after it was raised; prune() (lib/bridge-store.js, DELETE FROM bridge_outbound WHERE state IN ('delivered','dropped') AND updated_at < 30 days, no route condition) removes the row 30 days later whether or not its route is open; outbound.enqueueStatus guards only on NOT EXISTS (a status row for the route), and the gateway tick (lib/bridge-gateway.js, the PENDING_NOTICE_MS loop and the master-unavailable branch of advance) calls it for every open route on every pass. A route open for about 31 days therefore gets a second, fresh, ready status notice, and another every 31 days after. The same path re-raises a DELIVERED status notice 30 days after delivery. This contradicts the ruling (nothing let go may become a fresh notification), the code comment on expire(), the schema comment 'One status item per route, ever', and docs/operator-bridge.md ('A route's status notice that expired is not raised a second time'). test/bridge-retention.test.js checks this only two days out, before prune can act. Construction, not a longer list: make the guard read the fact that outlives the row - bridge_routes.pending_notice_at is already written by enqueueStatus and stays with the open route, so refuse when it is set - and add a test that expires the notice, runs prune() past 30 days with the route still open, and asserts enqueueStatus creates nothing. Search for the other members: every idempotency key whose only record is a bridge_outbound row that prune can delete while its cause is still open. Notifications are safe (the cause leaves the 24-hour lookback weeks before the key is pruned) and candidate items are safe (the candidate row is gone). Not checked here and outside this delta: the route failure notices keyed route:<id>:<what>, which prune also removes while a route is open.
findings.fix_cost: FIX buys a review round — this finding cites a judgeable file, so the fix moves the tree and re-opens coverage.

observations.summary: An approved operator-action candidate's 30-day limit coincides with the 30-day retention of its candidate row
observations.recommendation: Scope: instance - the outbound item is created with the candidate's decided_at, EXPIRY_MS.candidate['operator-action-required'] and RETENTION.decidedCandidateMs are both 30 days, and the bridge_candidates_delete_children trigger deletes a candidate's outbound items in any state. Today this is safe only because tick() calls expire() before prune() with the same clock, so the item is dropped and audited first. Three consequences: (1) if expire() throws (tick catches and continues), prune() deletes a still-ready item with no audit row; (2) the dropped row is not 'kept 30 days' as docs/operator-bridge.md's retention table says - it leaves at the next daily prune, and for a milestone it is kept 23 days, not 30; (3) the late-acknowledgement allowance (a helper that fetched before expiry and posts after) shrinks to under a day for operator-action items, after which the acknowledgement finds no row. No test runs prune() after expire(). If a commit is coming anyway: have prune() keep a decided candidate while it has a ready outbound item or one settled less than 30 days ago, and correct the table row.

observations.summary: A kind with no limit never expires, and nothing ties the limits table to the schema's lists
observations.recommendation: Scope: class - _outboundTtl returns null (never expires) for any notification type or candidate kind absent from EXPIRY_MS, and for a 'candidate' item whose candidate row is missing; the undecided-candidate loop skips on a missing entry too. All three notification types and both candidate kinds in lib/bridge-schema.js have entries today, and no type is doubled, so nothing is wrong now. The two reserved types (release-action-needed, certification-state-changed) would silently never expire when added. Failing towards 'kept' is the safe direction. observations.summary: A status row whose route has no pending_notice_at would make enqueueStatus throw

No released version wrote such a row (the bridge is not on main), no other writer of pending_notice_at exists, and the two statements are now one transaction, so this cannot arise from here on. ACCEPT unless a store written by the earlier branch code is going to be carried forward.
